items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Semiring R] {p : Polynomial R} {r : R} {n : ℕ},
  (p.comp (Polynomial.C r * Polynomial.X)).coeff n = p.coeff n * r ^ n
items.informal_description: For any semiring element $ r $ and natural number $ n $, the coefficient of $ X^n $ in the polynomial $ p(rX) $ is equal to the coefficient of $ X^n $ in $ p $ multiplied by $ r^n $.

items.informal_name: Multiplicativity of Taylor Series Expansion for Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] (r : R) (p q : Polynomial R),
  (Polynomial.taylor r) (p * q) = (Polynomial.taylor r) p * (Polynomial.taylor r) q
items.informal_description: For any polynomials $ p, q \in R[X] $ over a semiring $ R $, the Taylor series expansion at $ r \in R $ satisfies $ \operatorname{taylor}_r(p \cdot q) = \operatorname{taylor}_r(p) \cdot \operatorname{taylor}_r(q) $, where $ \operatorname{taylor}_r(f) $ denotes the polynomial obtained by substituting $ X + r $ into $ f $. This expresses that the Taylor expansion map preserves multiplication of polynomials.

items.type: {R : Type u_1} → [inst : Semiring R] → Polynomial R → R → Polynomial R
items.informal_description: For a polynomial $ p $ and scalar $ s $, the polynomial $ \text{scaleRoots}(p, s) $ is defined as the sum over all $ i $ in the support of $ p $ of the monomial $ i $ multiplied by the coefficient of $ p $ at $ i $ times $ s $ raised to the power of the natural degree of $ p $ minus $ i $. This operation scales the roots of $ p $ by the factor $ s $.

items.informal_name: Coefficient Scaling Identity: $ \text{coeff}_i(\text{scaleRoots}(p, s)) = \text{coeff}_i(p) \cdot s^{\text{natDegree}(p) - i} $
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (p : Polynomial R) (s : R) (i : ℕ),
  (p.scaleRoots s).coeff i = p.coeff i * s ^ (p.natDegree - i)
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ p $ over a semiring $ R $, scalar $ s \in R $, and natural number $ i $, the coefficient of $ X^i $ in the polynomial obtained by scaling the roots of $ p $ by $ s $ is equal to the coefficient of $ X^i $ in $ p $ multiplied by $ s $ raised to the power of the natural degree of $ p $ minus $ i $. The natural degree of $ p $ is defined as the degree of $ p $ if $ p $ is non-zero, and 0 otherwise.

items.informal_name: Scaling Roots of Constant Polynomials Leaves Them Unchanged
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (r c : R), (Polynomial.C c).scaleRoots r = Polynomial.C c
items.informal_description: For any elements $r$ and $c$ in a semiring $R$, scaling the roots of the constant polynomial $C(c)$ by $r$ results in the same constant polynomial $C(c)$. In symbols: $\text{scaleRoots}_r(C(c)) = C(c)$.
